Q1. Seal Part A for the 2027 refit, as an unscored diagnostic only. Convert both monthly TB3MS and daily DTB3 with the pinned formula BEY(d) = 100·365·(d/100)/(360 − 91·(d/100)), d in percent, fixed 91 days. Do not splice GS3M at 1981-09; that break sits between the high-rate onsets and the later sample and would confound the thing being measured. GS3M from 1981-09 is a check only (mean and max |BEY(TB3MS) − GS3M|), never an input. Outputs (1)–(3) as drafted, λ = 1, origins identity-asserted, episode-block bootstrap 1000 draws, seed 42, 10–90%. Add one reported table, not a criterion: mean (BEY curve − discount curve) by decade and by 3m-rate bins (0–4, 4–8, 8–12, >12). The level dependence is the point — gap 0.10 pp at 4%, 0.28 at 8%, 0.81 at 15% — and four of twelve onsets sit in the high-rate window where the discount curve understates inversion depth by several tenths of a point. At the local derivative (−1.6 pp of P per 10 bp) today’s 0.18 pp convention gap is ~3 pp of P; in 1980–81 it is an order larger. That is a real measurement defect. It is not a reason to touch frozen weights or to publish any BEY probability before a later council, a sealed spec, and that configuration’s own replay (§1.3). No automatic switch. Item (4), the refit-date BEY probability, stays inside `uscorede.konvention_bey` and off the dashboard.

Q2. Closed historically. B1/B2 are a second shot after a seen rejection (dLL −77.88 pp, 0% of LOEO folds positive, 192 origins). The missing-history penalty was in the sealed step-4 design; discovering that it dominates the number is not new economics. Rosenberg–Maurer was known, direction included, before that run. Power settles it: 8 onsets, MDE80 ≈ 2.8·SD_block, order 30 pp, so the likely print is “no difference,” which would launder a rejected feature back onto the agenda. Strike B1/B2 from the spec; do not leave them parked “in case.” If a future council is outvoted into running them anyway, the bar in the draft is not acceptable as written: 1.96·SD_block with ~8 episode blocks is a normal approximation on a sample that cannot support it; “neither crosses ⇒ incumbent stays” must be labelled a lock, not evidence of equivalence; the spec must print E3 in full and state that curve-only on the 1961Q3 panel is a different configuration from operational +20.37% (219) and may not be cited as it. B3 only, and narrower than drafted: after the ≥12-snapshot revision audit, an unscored ledger column may carry the bare expectations-minus-3m number from THREEFYTP10. No literature sentence, no “share of the curve,” no threshold, no count. A scored test waits on ≥2 post-sealing onsets and is decades away. That cost is the closed search working.

Q3. C5 stays, with one added sentence: the gap is not an input, and no alternative P is to be computed by substituting the CMT curve into the frozen weights. Without that sentence a reader does exactly the illegal substitution (discount +1.124 → 14.8%; CMT +0.95 fed into the same logit → ~17.9%) and treats 18% as the corrected figure. C6 as written fails the firewall. “98% is term premium; the literature says the expectations component is what predicts” is a directional claim that the operational signal is the non-predictive part, from one model (KW TP 0.99) on one day, against ACM at 0.84 two months earlier, on series that revise. Strip the 98% figure and the Rosenberg–Maurer sentence from the live note. What may remain under P: term-premium estimates are model-dependent and revised, and are not inputs. The economic argument belongs in the unsealed spec, not beside the number.

Q4. C2, C3, C4: ratify. C2 closes a §1.2 breach; C3 states the spread actually used; C4 replaces a false “advance” label. Pin the C4 rule as quarter-end + 32 + 10 days so “later vintage” cannot be widened after the next awkward print. C1: ratify ex post, and this is acceptable despite being post hoc, because it is a label, the old label was false at +1.4 bp, and it cannot move P, the band, the verdict, or the ignition column. Disclose in the same sentence that 5 bp was set after seeing +1.4 bp. Freeze `MAERKE_MIN_DK` until the 2027 refit; a retune after the next flat month is a second fork. C7’s gate label (“F5 +23.2% vs curve-only +27.1%, same full path”) is correct and should stay. The bootstrap interval does not stay where it was put. It is the oracle-censored 198-origin interval, mean +0.120 nats, 90% [−0.042, +0.239], 8.9% of draws ≤ 0. Parking that under the §1.2 sentence attaches uncertainty to figure (ii) only and makes the censored number the one with statistical standing. Either compute and print the same episode-block interval for oracle-free +20.37% (219) in the same slot, same draw count and pinned seed, or move the censored interval to a footnote that says it attaches to (ii) only and is not the uncertainty of the lead figure. Do not leave it as drafted.

Q5. No change to the verdict string. “Not distinguishable” stays in the verdict, the ledger, and the dashboard. The paired supplement this month is [−6.5, −0.4] pp and the backtest disagrees on 12/198, always with the paired rule saying distinguishable and the band saying not. That is the band rule being more conservative, which is why it is the rule. A dashboard gloss of “no robust signal under the band rule” is a second verdict in plain language. One methods sentence may record the 12/198 fact and the direction of every disagreement. It does not appear on the verdict line.

Claude, as written, amended, or struck. Q1: amend. Seal Part A, convert-both, no splice, no automatic switch — that part stands. Strike |Δ oracle-free| < 2 pp as anything a reader could treat as a test; a level-dependent gap of 0.8 pp in the Volcker window makes 2 pp of skill a wish, not a bound. If the sentence survives, it is labelled “author’s prior, not a criterion,” and it is not printed next to the result. Q2: amend by deletion. “Only B3” stands; “B1/B2 listed only because” does not — listing them is the second shot half-authorized. The EBP analogy is rhetoric; the closure reason to write down is a seen rejection plus forking paths, not §8.2 by nickname. Q3: C5 keep with the anti-substitution sentence. C6 as Claude amended (keep 98%, add model-dependence) is struck; model-dependence replaces the 98% and the literature sentence, it does not accompany them. Q4: C1–C4 as Claude says, plus the freeze on 5 bp; C7 interval placement struck and replaced as above. Q5: keep as written.

Biggest risk in this proposal. Item (4) and a B3 column, even unscored and even off the manifest hash, become the alternative model the moment they diverge from P. Today’s illegal CMT substitution is already ~3 pp; a BEY refit probability printed anywhere a screenshot can reach will be cited as the real P, which is a §1.3 breach by distribution rather than by code. The mitigation is physical: BEY P never renders on the dashboard or in LOG.md, and the expectations column, if it ever exists, is a bare number with no sentence next to it.
message.reasoning:
I am Grok 4.7, preparing my independent proposal for the council.

I am treating this as a senior macro-econometrician. I will answer each agenda question independently, scrutinize Claude's draft positions hard, and be concrete and quantitative. Key constraints include: nothing changes before the September 2027 refit, weights are frozen, RAADETS_2027 governs, feature search is closed, and context lines are firewalled. Every number is already known, so I will judge whether decisions are acceptable despite being post hoc. For Q1 Part A, convention sensitivity depends on level: the discount versus bond-equivalent gap varies with the level of the instrument.

The discount-to-bond-equivalent gap is large at high rates, reaching 0.28–0.81 percentage points in the 1970s and 1980s. The standard conversion formula is correct: BEY = 365·d / (360 − 91·d). I agree with Claude’s Part A proposal to seal the drafted positions, convert both TB3MS and DTB3 with one pinned formula, use CMT post-1981 only as a check, preregister |Δ oracle-free WF| < 2 pp, and avoid automatic switching.

Splicing GS3M from 1981-09 would create a level break exactly where the high-rate regime ends. That is a bad idea.

The 2 pp preregistered bound is not obvious. The current gap is 0.18 pp, which implies roughly 2.9 pp on P under linear sensitivity. But skill loss is not linear in level shifts. A level-dependent bias that is larger during high-rate onsets could move skill more than a constant shift. I should not rubber-stamp the 2 pp limit without further thought.

The convention mismatch is a genuine defect. The feature is not the economic object the literature studies, and the distortion is correlated with rate level and recession regimes. §1.3 assigns figures to their producing configuration, so frozen weights until 2027 make an unscored sensitivity at the refit the right instrument. Switching now would break frozen weights. The open question is whether the council should address this beyond an unscored sensitivity.

The 2027 refit will use a sealed replay to judge whether the sensitivity is material. This keeps the council from pre-committing to switch. The 2 pp preregistered figure should be treated as a disclosed prior, not a decision gate.

If the sensitivity gap turns out to be 3 pp, the council must publish it without invoking the preregistered bound as a decision gate. The pinned 91-day convention is correct; actual T-bill maturities vary and should not be interpolated. I am also checking the exact formula notation in the brief.

The conversion formula checks out numerically. I will approve Part A with the amendment that the 2 pp bound is a disclosed prior belief, not a decision criterion.

I will add a diagnostic breakdown of the paired difference by decade or rate-level bin so the level dependence is visible in the output. λ stays at 1, and the identity-of-origins assertion is correct. No live corrected P will be produced before the refit; that would violate the firewall and §1.3. Q2 Part B is the hard one.

The ACM test was sealed and rejected at dLL −77.88 pp. Claude attributes this to a missing-history penalty rather than the economic hypothesis itself. This is a fair reading of the design, but re-opening the test requires new economic rationale plus council mandate and a sealed specification. Claiming the prior result was contaminated by a penalty is methodological, not new economics.

The Rosenberg-Maurer economics was known before the test. The pre-1961 penalty was also known. Running B1/B2 now is a second shot after seeing a catastrophic result and constructing a story for why it does not count. The EBP precedent in §8.2 applies because the onset pattern has been seen. But ACM differs from EBP: it was a feature ablation with a known design flaw.

The forking-paths logic is exactly why the search was closed. Power is too low to distinguish the eight onsets, so B1/B2 will almost certainly return a null that launders the rejected idea back onto the agenda. A second look contaminates further and produces the worst outcome: a null that survives. B3 as a prospective unscored test is the cleanest remaining option, though it still carries contamination from known literature direction and step 4 numbers.

Claude’s proposed context line uses Kim-Wright daily data from 1990. This avoids rehabilitating the rejected ACM monthly series, which ends in July 2026. §8.3 requires a sealed prospective test to have no pre-2027 evidence and at least two post-sealing onsets; an unscored tracking line needs at least twelve snapshot revisions.

C6 already embeds the Rosenberg-Maurer expectation-prediction claim in its dashboard, which creates a firewall problem under Q3. B3 institutionalizes that same unvalidated directional signal. I will close the historical retest and refuse B1/B2. B3 is too narrow for my taste.

I am now testing whether an unscored context line can exist without violating the firewall. §8.3 permits a bare number after revision audit, provided it carries no interpretive sentence linking it to recession probability and never appears adjacent to P in a way that invites subtraction. The real question is whether C6 or B3 undercuts the firewall in practice by telling the reader that P is too low.

I will remove any interpretive literature sentence from a live context line. If B3 is adopted, only the bare number remains, and the revision audit must precede any ledger column. B1 and B2 are not authorized; they should not be listed as available options in the sealed specification.

C5 is a factual convention note. It does not tell the reader which way P is wrong in a predictive sense.

The 0.18 pp gap quantifies the distortion. Because the discount 3-month rate is lower than its CMT equivalent, the discount curve is wider and more positive than a CMT-consistent curve. That steeper positive curve pushes P downward. The current discount curve yields P at 14.8%.

C5 is fair and should stay, provided it explicitly warns readers not to invert the gap into an alternative P. C6 is worse because it embeds an unvalidated directional claim that 98% of the curve is term premium.

The literature argument in C6 is now clearer. It claims the model reads only the sum of components, not the expectations piece that actually predicts recessions. Today expectations minus 3-month is +0.02 versus DTB3, while the curve shows +1.01 of term premium. Rosenberg-Maurer says term premium does not predict, so the current signal may be overestimating the recession risk.

C6 functions as a second unofficial verdict that P is spurious or too low. The 98% term-premium figure is model-dependent and one-day-specific; both series revise. I will keep C5 but add a one-line prohibition against computing an alternative P from the convention gap. I will also strip the Rosenberg-Maurer predictive claim and the 98% framing from the live dashboard.

The 98% term-premium figure is arithmetic for one day and one model, so publishing it next to P is an unvalidated signal. The literature prediction sentence belongs in the specification, not under live P. Claude’s proposed model-dependence note replaces the literature claim rather than adding to it.

C1 sets a 5 bp threshold after observing +1.4 bp.

The 5 bp threshold is post hoc but acceptable if the selection is disclosed. It is arbitrary, yet it correctly suppresses daily noise. A 1.4 bp monthly shift is roughly three times the typical daily curve movement, so the cutoff is calibrated to swallow normal volatility.

The 5 bp threshold is a label hack. The brief lacks the historical standard deviation of monthly curve changes, so inventing one would be arbitrary. A rule without a tuned constant is preferable.

The 5 bp threshold is acceptable post hoc because the prior label wrongly described a +1 bp shift as bear steepening. It must be pinned at 5 bp, disclosed as post-hoc, and forbidden from retuning before the 2027 refit. C2 fixes a §1.2 breach and must be ratified. C3 is factual and should be kept.

C4 corrects a false label and should be ratified. The +32+10 day rule must be stated as the operational definition of "later than advance" so it is not quietly widened.

C7 fixes the 3.9 versus 2.5 confusion by pairing both numbers on the same path. The 4.4 paired loss-bootstrap interval belongs under the §1.2 sentence.

Review 2 shows mean improvement of +0.120 nats, or +27.1% of base-rate log-loss. The 90% interval is [−0.042; +0.239]. Eight point-nine percent of draws are at or below zero. Nine cycle blocks were observed. The oracle-censored 198-origin set was used.

The §1.2 order lists three figures: oracle-free +20.37% (219), oracle-censored +27.05% (198), and nested λ +18.32% (198). The clause forbids the oracle-censored figure from appearing as a standalone public number.

Printing the bootstrap interval under the §1.2 sentence gives that figure statistical standing. That is the opposite of the clause's intent. The interval includes zero, so it deflates the +27.05 figure. Placement matters.

The bootstrap interval is an uncertainty statement for the oracle-censored figure, not a fourth skill figure. A careful reader is fine with it under the sentence, but a dashboard reader may see +27.1% with an interval and the other two as bare points. The interval should either be computed for the oracle-free figure too, or placed so it cannot be read as the headline’s uncertainty.

Review 2 asked to show the historical paired loss bootstrap next to the skill figures. Showing it only for the censored set violates the spirit of §1.2's order even if the sentence itself is intact.

Position: Ratify C7's gate labelling. Do not ratify the interval placement as-is.

Either the oracle-free +20.37% figure must carry an identical block-bootstrap interval in the same visual slot, or the censored interval must move to a footnote explicitly stating it applies only to figure (ii). The brief does not show that the oracle-free interval was actually computed.

If the oracle-free interval is not computed before ratification, the interval should be struck from under the §1.2 sentence and placed in an appendix explicitly labeled as applying only to figure (ii). The phrase "4.4 paired loss-bootstrap interval" likely refers to a document item or label, not a literal figure.

The paired supplement under the band rule is a descriptive bracket, not a verdict modifier. The 12 backtest disagreements between paired and band rules are a feature of the conservative band logic, not a bug to narrate around.

Review 1 wants the dashboard to read "no robust signal" while the ledger keeps "not distinguishable." That would create two competing public verdicts from one underlying rule.

The dashboard must keep the sealed phrase "not distinguishable" and reject any parallel gloss. A footnote claiming the paired interval is entirely negative would still create a second verdict, so no competing plain-language description should be added.

The 12 backtest disagreements between paired and band rules can be disclosed once in a methodology note, not in the dashboard verdict string. Claude’s Q5 should remain unchanged.

For Q1, I will amend the positions verdict to seal Part A, convert both series, and forbid splicing or automatic switching.

For Q1, the |Δ|<2pp threshold must be struck or explicitly labeled as an author's prior, not a test. The diagnostic output should also include a decade or rate-bin mean gap.

For Q2, B1 and B2 should be deleted from the specification entirely rather than merely listed as exceptions. B3 is narrower than Claude's draft: it uses a bare number after revision audit, omits the literature sentence, and drops the 98% framing. THREEFYTP10 remains acceptable for the series.

The EBP closure reason must be framed as forking paths after a seen rejection, not merely as an EBP analogy, to prevent future councils from claiming §8.2 does not apply.

For Q3, C5 should keep its anti-alternative-P sentence; C6 should strike the 98% framing and the Rosenberg-Maurer predictive claim from the live note, since Claude’s amendment is insufficient.

The biggest risk is that an unscored BEY sensitivity sitting next to the operational P will be read as a second probability and a sanctioned alternative model. The unscored BEY P must be kept strictly inside the diagnostic artifact, never on the dashboard beside the operational figure.

The closed search carries a concrete cost: if the missing-history penalty buried a real effect, it will not be known until two post-2027 onsets, roughly a decade. This is the correct price of closing the search. The logit calculation was verified and yields about 14.8%.

The CMT-style +0.95 curve yields about 17.9% probability. The gap from the operational curve is roughly +3.1 percentage points. The derivative is approximately −1.6 points per 10 basis points. This illegal substitution figure should be used only to quantify the temptation, not recommended for publication.

At a 15% discount rate the curve gap is 0.81 percentage points. In 1981 the three-month rate was near 14–16%, so a constant two-point skill bound is too coarse. A one-basis-point overstatement of the curve shifts the logit index by roughly 1.05, which is large enough to change the verdict. In inverted high-rate regimes the discount curve is less inverted than the BEY curve because the three-month discount rate sits below the three-month BEY rate.

The discount convention understates inversion depth in high-rate periods, so it may understate the recession signal exactly at 1980 and 1981. Four of the twelve onsets fall in this regime. This is the actual defect. An unscored sensitivity remains the correct response because the weights are frozen and §1.3 requires a sealed replay before any figure is claimed for a new configuration.

The council should pre-commit that the 2027 refit specification must include Part A as a mandatory diagnostic. Any convention switch would be treated as a separate sealed configuration with its own replay, not as a footnote to the refit.

If B1 and B2 are outvoted, the symmetric bar is unacceptable without changes.

The 1.96 threshold is theatrical precision; with only eight onsets and nine blocks the normal approximation is poor.

The rule that "neither crosses → curve-only stays" is an asymmetry of outcome. Because the minimum detectable effect is roughly thirty percentage points, the test is designed to return "no difference" and the lock preserves the incumbent. This is acceptable as a safeguard, but it must not be described as evidence of equivalence.

The specification must fully cite E3: the previous dLL gap was seventy-seven point eight eight percentage points, zero positive folds, and the secondary truncated comparison never ran. This run is a second shot after seeing that number.

The 1961Q3 panel drops four onsets, including 1953 and 1957. The curve-only baseline is therefore a different configuration from the operational model and cannot be cited as its skill. Automatic adoption remains prohibited; only an agenda trigger is permitted.
